_readme: The custom nodes baked into the R&D pod image — DATA, not Dockerfile ARGs, so the
launcher can add and remove them from /comfyui without a repo checkout (ComfyUI Node
Manager Phase 2; see docs/design/comfyui-node-manager.md).
Edited two ways, and both end as a commit on main: by hand here, or by the /comfyui
node table, which resolves a repo URL to its tip SHA and writes this file through the
GitHub contents API. Git stays the source of truth either way — an image must always
be reproducible from `git checkout <sha> && docker build`.
`sha` is REQUIRED for every cloned node and is a 12-char commit id. Never a branch:
a floating ref means a plain rebuild can change generation behaviour with no commit
of ours, which is the drift the pinning work of 2026-08-19 exists to prevent. (12
chars, not 40, because a full hex sha trips this repo's secret scanner.)
`vendored: true` entries are NOT cloned — they are COPY'd from ./custom_nodes/ by the
Dockerfile. They are listed here so one file answers 'what is on the image', which is
what the panel shows; the Dockerfile skips them.
`skipRequirements` names folders whose requirements.txt is deliberately NEVER installed.
`noClasses: true` means the pack registers no NODE CLASSES — it is a frontend or UI
extension. The panel checks each node against what a live pod actually loaded, and that
check reads /object_info, which only ever sees packs that register classes. Without this
flag such a pack reads as 'not seen' forever, and an expected warning is how people learn
to ignore warnings.
`prod: true` also bakes the node into the SERVERLESS WORKER (services/atlas-serverless),
which is the Atlas Maker generation path. Most nodes are R&D-only and stay off it: some
are licence-encumbered (PuLID-Flux2 needs non-commercial antelopev2), some are simply not
needed in prod. Promotion is DELIBERATE — the standing rule is to promote only after a
pod off the R&D image renders clean, and a blueprint using an unpromoted node will not
run in the Atlas Maker.
`corePacks` names packs that ship INSIDE ComfyUI itself and live under its custom_nodes
folder. A pod reports them like any other pack, so without this the panel would flag them
as "not in the image" forever — true, useless, and the kind of standing false alarm that
teaches people to ignore the real ones.

nodes.name: ComfyUI_IPAdapter_plus
nodes.note: IPAdapter. Dormant upstream since April 2025; survived the v0.33.1 core bump.

nodes.name: PuLID_ComfyUI
nodes.note: The SDXL Pulid* nodes, incl. PulidModelLoader used by Characterdesignertest3.

nodes.name: ComfyUI_essentials
nodes.note: MaskBlur+, SimpleMath+, ImageCompositeFromMaskBatch+ — used by the SAM3 background-removal graph, which had them only because ONE artist box did. This sha is the one that graph was authored against, read off the node properties in its export. In skipRequirements: its five requirements (numba, colour-science, rembg, pixeloe, transparent-background) are ALL unpinned, and rembg would pull a CPU onnxruntime alongside the onnxruntime-gpu the face stack installs explicitly. Verified safe to skip at this sha — every one of those is imported lazily inside the single node that uses it (rembg in RemBGSession.execute, transparent_background in TransparentBGSession.execute, colour in ImageApplyLUT.execute, pixeloe in PixelOEPixelize.execute); module level is only torch/numpy/scipy/PIL/kornia, all of which ComfyUI core already ships. Those four nodes will fail at execute time, nothing else.

nodes.name: ComfyUI-PuLID-Flux2
nodes.note: PuLID for FLUX.2. R&D ONLY — needs InsightFace antelopev2, non-commercial. Fragile: monkey-patches block.forward and model_function_wrapper, and its last commit predates our core pin. Its requirements.txt is in skipRequirements.

nodes.name: ComfyUI-VideoHelperSuite
nodes.note: Video load / combine / preview. Upstream publishes NO tags, so this is a master SHA. Imports comfy_api.v0_0_2 IO.MatchType at module level — a core bump can break it at IMPORT, not at render.

nodes.name: ComfyUI-Manager
nodes.note: Security level middle, pre-seeded by the Dockerfile. Do NOT let it 'Update ComfyUI' — that patches the ephemeral container only. Registers no node classes (it is a UI extension), so it never appears in /object_info — confirmed on a live pod.

nodes.name: ComfyUI-PuLID-Flux
nodes.note: The artist's MODIFIED PuLID-Flux. Cloning stock balazik would drop the attn_mask fix and break the blueprint. See custom_nodes/README.md.

nodes.name: ComfyUI-Invisible-ErrorRecall
nodes.note: Ours, frontend-only: re-surfaces a run's error on the failing node when the /ws socket dropped.

nodes.name: ComfyUI-SemanticLayers
nodes.note: Ours, nodes-only, no third-party deps: routes a layered decomposer's variable layer batch onto fixed semantic outputs. Already COPY'd by both Dockerfiles — listed here because this file is what sync-local-nodes.py and the /comfyui panel read, and its absence is why neither could see the pack. It is on NO registry and has no git url, so nothing can INSTALL it: Manager's 'install missing nodes' returns empty and there is nothing to clone. It reaches a machine only as files. Unlisted until 2026-09-15, which is how the artist's box ended up without it while carrying every other pack.
